scenario_prompt: Write a two-paragraph executive summary addressed directly to a fictional buyer's Chief Financial Officer, recommending a cloud migration. Context: a mid-market freight brokerage firm is moving its load-matching and carrier-settlement systems off on-premises Microsoft SQL Server (28 instances) running on Hyper-V (620 virtual machines) onto Google Cloud, targeting Google Compute Engine for compute and Cloud SQL for PostgreSQL for the data layer, over a 2-year, $4,200,000 programme. The CFO has stated she is measured on reducing the current $1,850,000 annual technology spend and on a clean DOT compliance audit, which opens in 6 months. Cover why this matters to her now and what she should expect from the programme. Return only the summary text, two paragraphs, no headers.
text:
This is an executive summary. What customer source material do I have for this — any RFP text, discovery notes, or direct quotes from the CFO beyond what's in your message? I'll proceed with the draft now using only what you've given me; unsupplied figures will be marked as gaps rather than invented.

**Executive summary**

To Chief Financial Officer:

You are measured on cutting your current $1,850,000 annual technology spend and on a clean DOT compliance audit that opens in six months. Today, your load-matching and carrier-settlement systems run on 28 on-premises Microsoft SQL Server instances hosted across 620 Hyper-V virtual machines [PF-2.13 GAP: current annual run-rate cost attributable specifically to this SQL Server/Hyper-V estate, as distinct from the $1,850,000 total technology spend — not supplied]. We propose migrating this estate to Google Cloud over a 2-year, $4,200,000 programme, moving compute to Google Compute Engine and the data layer to Cloud SQL for PostgreSQL. This shift replaces fixed on-premises infrastructure you own and patch yourself with managed compute and database services Google operates and secures [PF-2.14 REVIEW (commitment): "secures" reads as a security commitment — confirm the intended scope of Google's shared-responsibility boundary before this ships].

Over the six months before your audit opens, you should expect the programme to prioritize the carrier-settlement systems and their supporting data, since auditors will scrutinize financial-transaction integrity and access controls first [PF-2.14 REVIEW (commitment): sequencing carrier-settlement work ahead of the audit reads as a delivery commitment — confirm the migration plan actually front-loads this scope before promising it]. You should also expect a documented cutover and rollback plan for each of the 28 SQL Server instances, since an audit that opens mid-migration needs evidence of controlled change, not evidence of disruption [PF-3.3: DOT compliance audit, retained — buyer's stated term]. Beyond the audit window, the $4,200,000 investment is the basis for measuring progress against your $1,850,000 annual spend target [PF-2.4 GAP: the expected post-migration annual run-rate, payback period, or specific cost reduction — not supplied]; we recommend tracking actual infrastructure spend monthly against this baseline so you can show your board the trajectory, not just the endpoint.

## Unresolved before this document is sent

| Marker | Rule | What is needed |
|---|---|---|
| Current annual run-rate cost of the 28 SQL Server instances / 620 VMs | PF-2.13 | The portion of the $1,850,000 total spend attributable to this specific on-prem estate, so the migration's savings claim can be quantified against a real baseline |
| "Google...secures" | PF-2.14 | Confirmation this doesn't overstate Google's responsibility under the shared-responsibility model, or a rewrite scoping it to what Google actually manages |
| Prioritizing carrier-settlement systems ahead of the audit | PF-2.14 | Confirmation the actual migration sequencing front-loads this scope, or this should be restated as a recommendation rather than an expectation |
| Post-migration annual run-rate / cost reduction target | PF-2.4 | The expected savings figure or payback period, so the CFO has a number to hold the programme to, not just a total spend |
